pages.title: Wall Street analyst sets Apple stock price target for 12 months
pages.text:
As Apple Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL) stock regained bullish momentum over the past 30 days through September 17 – fueled by its strong fiscal results, key leadership updates, and the unveiling of its latest product lineup – Wamsi Mohan, a Wall Street analyst at Bank of America Corp. (NYSE: BAC), expects a rally towards a new all-time high (ATH) over the next 12 months.
Mohan reiterated a ‘Buy’ rating for Apple stock and reaffirmed the bank’s 12-month price target for AAPL at $370. With AAPL stock trading at $334.28 on Thursday, BofA signals a potential 10.69% upside.
This firm reiterated a bullish outlook for Apple stock over the next 12 months driven by the aggressive promotions from U.S. wireless carriers, which effectively neutralize higher device pricing and catalyze iPhone sales.
Mohan highlighted that maximum trade-in allowances have expanded up to $1,200 for the iPhone 18 Pro Max. This is paired with flexible 36-month financing structures and remarkably lenient condition requirements across AT&T Inc. (NYSE: T), Verizon Communications Inc. (NYSE: VZ), and T-Mobile US, Inc. (NASDAQ: TMUS).
Beyond immediate hardware dynamics, BofA argued that Apple stock presents an exceptional long-term investment profile grounded in the company’s disciplined financial execution and structural technology advantages.
The analyst’s note added that the company’s massive capital return program continuously enhances shareholder value, while its strategic positioning ensures market leadership in deploying on-device AI capabilities directly at the edge.
Coupled with unexploited optionality across upcoming product categories and expansion markets, he believes that Apple remains uniquely capitalized to drive sustained earnings growth and outperform market expectations.
Is Apple a good stock to buy?
At the time of writing, 32 Wall Street analysts surveyed by TipRanks over the past three months, have set an average rating of ‘Moderate Buy’ for Apple stock. Additionally, these analysts have an average target for the next 12 months of $336.26, suggesting a possible rally to a new ATH.
Apple stock forecast for the next 12 months. Source: TipRanks
The highest 12-month price target for AAPL from the sampled analysts is $400, while the lowest is $245.
Over the past 12 months, AAPL’s price has rallied 40.54%. As a result, the company’s market capitalization is hovering at $4.9 trillion at the time of publication.
If AAPL’s price continues with its 12-month established uptrend, largely influenced by the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, these bullish targets could be achieved.

pages.title: Apple's Market Value Grew From $350 Billion to $4.75 Trillion During Tim Cook's 15 Years as CEO. Here's What That Growth Curve Means for Betting on Apple's Next Chapter Under John Ternus. | The Motley Fool
pages.text:
▲ S&P 500 +---%|▲ Stock Advisor +---%Join The Motley Fool
Tim Cook had enormous shoes to fill when he took over the Apple (AAPL +0.22%) CEO role from Steve Jobs in 2011. Jobs was a visionary leader, and skeptics weren't sure Cook was the right person to lead the consumer tech company into its next chapter. Fifteen years later, and the proof is in the pudding: Over Cook's tenure, the tech giant experienced massive growth as its market cap ballooned from $350 billion to approximately $4.75 trillion.
John Ternus took over from Cook on Sept. 1, and as his time at the helm of Apple begins, he faces the same sort of questions. Long-term investors want to know: Can Ternus match Cook's incredible run? How will the growth curve bend now?
New Apple CEO John Ternus. Image source: Apple.
Apple is in terrific shape, and that's both good and bad news for Ternus. The company is a well-oiled machine, but expectations will remain elevated. In its fiscal third quarter, revenue grew 16% year over year. The growth was driven by iPhone sales that rose 21.7% and services revenue that rose 12%. Total revenue reached $109.4 billion.
$4.9TMarket cap calculated using publicly traded shares outstanding only. Does not include unlisted, private, or dual-class non-traded shares. Implied market cap may vary.
Ternus is inheriting a business with immense recurring, high-margin, and diversified revenue. The downside is that the company's latest revenue guidance was fairly muted -- only 9% to 11% for the current quarter -- as management anticipates intensifying supply constraints. This will mark Ternus' first challenge, and investors will closely watch how he navigates this period.
There's also the problem with China. Under Cook, Apple became extremely reliant on Chinese manufacturing. Ternus will need to work through geopolitical tensions, the need to geographically diversify its manufacturing footprint, and U.S. pressure to onshore more of its manufacturing. And there are plenty of questions about Apple's long-term position in the artificial intelligence race.
The good news is that Ternus is a 25-year Apple veteran and has had a front-row seat to all that the iPhone maker has endured over the last quarter-century. If the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra (priced at more than $2,000) are successful, those will be not only morale wins but also economic ones.
Duplicating Cook's run won't be easy. I'd expect Ternus to usher in a new era of steady, but dialed-back growth over the next several years. A return to a focus on excellent design and innovation will be the real mark of success for the engineer-turned-executive.
Apple isn't a young, scrappy tech start-up. It's one of the largest companies in the world, and its cash-generating ability is astounding. It's still worth investing in, but it's not the growth stock it once was, and that's OK.

Apple (AAPL) Trading Above Analyst Targets as Memory Costs Crimp Margin Outlook
Apple shares have lapped analyst price targets while memory costs quietly eat into margins, and a $1,999 folding phone debut is about to test whether the market's goodwill toward a new CEO holds up.
Published October 6, 2026, 8:35am ET · 3 min read
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
A prominent green bull and an upward trending stock chart illustrate the potential for significant growth in Apple stock, reflecting the article's focus on investment returns. © Shutterstock
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL | AAPL Price Prediction) shareholders face an unusual problem because the stock has risen past the forecasts of the analysts who cover it. Apple closed at $332.89, which is above the $328.09 average analyst price target. Apple has caught up to a full year of expected appreciation, and most analysts have not raised their numbers yet.
If we look at price targets issued in only the past few months, the average is higher at $334.90. Regardless, AAPL stock is getting close.
A target under the share price means estimates are stale relative to the rally, and analysts will likely raise targets to match the price unless results disappoint, in which case downgrades become more likely. Apple is up 22.79% this year, compared with 13.62% for the S&P 500, extending the valuation.
A Wide Target Range Shows a Street That Can’t Agree
44 analysts cover Apple, and their targets range from $215 to $405. For a mature company, a range this wide suggests analysts disagree about what Apple is: some see a hardware maker facing rising costs, while others see a services and artificial intelligence platform that deserves a premium.
The median target is at $340, above both the average and share price. A few low outliers pull the mean down. The average fiscal 2027 earnings estimate has slid to $9.5758 per share from $9.6826 three months ago, meaning the rally happened while earnings expectations drifted lower.
Rising Memory Costs Are the Margin Risk Analysts Are Starting to Flag
Morgan Stanley cut its target to $355 from $360. It kept an Overweight rating, citing “limited upside… after a strong six-month run.” The bank also pointed to lower-than-expected iPhone pricing and sharply higher memory chip costs.
Memory costs are the bigger issue. Demand from artificial intelligence has pushed chip prices into an upcycle, and Apple buys a great deal of memory. On the July earnings call, Tim Cook described memory pricing as a “100-year flood”.
Excluding tariff refunds, gross margin fell to 48.1% in the June quarter from 49.3% in March, and September guidance points to a 46.5% midpoint. Management said memory accounted for more than that decline, and it expects help from carry-in inventory to shrink after September. That margin pressure exists no matter how many phones Apple sells.
Paying 36 Times Forward Earnings for a Folding Phone
Apple is trading at about 36 times forward earnings, compared with a trailing multiple of about 43x. That gap shows the market already expects strong profit growth, even though Apple guided September-quarter revenue growth to 9% to 11%.
The iPhone Duo, Apple’s first folding phone, is priced at $1,999 and goes on sale Oct. 23. Bloomberg reports that a smart home product is due Oct. 13.
The market expects Apple to sell about 6 million units of the Duo this year. Apple has more than 2.5 billion active devices, and its iPhone line brought in $54.3 billion in the June quarter alone. Next to numbers that size, a first-generation folding phone matters more for the brand than for revenue.
Apple hit an all-time high of $345.34 on Sept. 22, three weeks after John Ternus took over as chief executive. New leaders often get the benefit of the doubt until their first earnings report. Apple’s market value of about $4.86 trillion is also close to the $5 trillion mark. Some of the current multiple likely shows goodwill toward a leadership change whose results have not been tested yet.
What Could Change the Outlook for Apple Stock Before Earnings
Apple looks fully valued at this price. The business is excellent, but the stock already reflects a year of gains while memory costs push margins lower.
The Duo launch and the earnings report scheduled for Oct. 29, which Apple has not confirmed, could change my view. Apple would need strong early Duo demand. It would also need gross margin at or above its 47% to 48% guidance and a December-quarter outlook that shows memory costs under control.
Results like that would push targets higher. If margins slid instead, the next round of analyst changes is more likely to be downgrades.
Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) trades at a trailing earnings multiple of about 29. Azure grew 43% last quarter, and Microsoft Cloud revenue rose 27% to $59.3 billion. That growth comes from enterprise cloud and AI contracts, so it depends much less on smartphone upgrade cycles.

Apple Reportedly Partners With LG Electronics To Enter Smart Home Device Market
Apple Inc. has reportedly partnered with LG Electronics Inc. to co-develop a range of smart home accessories, aiming to revitalize its HomeKit ecosystem and challenge rivals Amazon and Google.
After the partial renovation and upgrade of the Apple Store, headphones, HomePod, phone cases, accessories, and other products are placed on the wall around the store, September 4, 2023, Shanghai, China. (Photo by Costfoto/NurPhoto via Getty Images)
Apple and LG have co-developed a new suite of smart hardware, including video doorbells, smart thermostats, indoor and outdoor security cameras, and smart locks.
While Apple oversees engineering and design, LG will sell the devices under its brand and handle manufacturing and customer support.
Apple is set to launch its own core hardware on Oct. 13, while the LG co-developed accessories are expected to release in the coming months following regulatory approvals.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
Apple Inc. (AAPL) is teaming up with LG Electronics Inc. to develop a broad suite of smart home hardware as part of a major initiative to revamp its presence in the connected home market, according to a Bloomberg News report.
The collaboration includes co-developing accessories such as a video doorbell, a smart thermostat, indoor and outdoor security cameras, a floodlight camera, and a smart deadbolt lock. While Apple helped direct design and engineering, the hardware will carry LG's branding, with the South Korean electronics firm handling manufacturing and ongoing product service.
AAPL stock added 0.2% on Tuesday and inched 0.1% in extended trading.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
The partnership utilizes a strategy Apple has previously employed with companies like Belkin and Logitech. By guiding external hardware development without taking on direct manufacturing or customer support costs, Apple can rapidly build an ecosystem around its platform.
The co-developed LG accessories will integrate into Apple’s broader smart home hub strategy and work alongside upcoming Apple-branded hardware. Apple is scheduled to introduce its new proprietary products, including a refreshed HomePod mini and an updated Apple TV set-top box on Oct. 13.
Regulatory filings with the U.S. Federal Communications Commission and certification organization UL Solutions show LG recently sought approval for the new hardware lineup. Public databases list products including the LG Video Doorbell Wired, LG Smart Thermostat, LG Smart Deadbolt Lock, and multiple camera models.
Advertisement|Remove ads.
The upcoming devices support popular industry connectivity standards, including Thread and Matter, as well as Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. The LG smart lock is also set to feature ultra-wideband (UWB) technology, enabling automatic unlocking functionality as a user approaches.
The ambitious rollout marks a formal overhaul of Apple’s HomeKit platform, launched in 2014 but struggling to gain market share against dominant offerings from Amazon.com Inc. and Alphabet Inc.’s Google.
For LG, the launch expands its footprint into key home hardware categories, marking its first outdoor camera, doorbell, and thermostat releases in recent years, alongside its first international smart lock release outside South Korea.

pages.title: Apple event 2026: Folding iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro, added AI features and more
pages.text:
Apple event 2026 recap: iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro, and more
Apple unveils its first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo
Apple saved the best for last at its biggest launch event of the year on Wednesday, unveiling the foldable iPhone Duo.
CEO John Ternus made his big debut, unveiling the iPhone 18 Pro, Airpods 5 and Apple Watch Series 12 before getting to the Duo, the company's first foldable iPhone.
Apple showcased a new set of colors for the iPhone 18, which comes in glacier and burgundy, following in the success of last year's electric Cosmic Orange colorway.
First impressions of the iPhone Duo — Apple's biggest iPhone redesign ever
Customers are looking at a premium price for Apple's latest devices, with the iPhone 18 Pro and Max getting a $100 hike over last year's models. The foldable Duo starts at $1,999.
The company raised prices on Macs and iPads over the summer as memory and storage costs have soared.
What you need to know:
Apple's first foldable iPhone starts at $1,999
Apple Watch is listening to your conversations
You will be paying $100 more for iPhone 18 Pro
AI image check with Apple Reference Image
The first product launch is the iPhone 18 Pro and Max in new colors
Ternus says the iPhone is the best device for AI
Apple Event product unveil on Sept. 9th, 2026.
Apple Inc.
Thanks for following the action with us!
Big shoutout to all the readers who joined us today. Thanks for hanging out and following along with the latest announcements from Apple.
We'll have more coverage of Apple's announcements on CNBC TV with analyst and trader reactions. Watch in real time on CNBC+ or the CNBC Pro stream.
C2 modem in iPhone Duo further reduces Apple's reliance on Qualcomm
A man records images of the new foldable iPhone Duo on display during Apple's event at the Steve Jobs Theater in Cupertino, California, U.S. Sept. 9, 2026.
Apple just unveiled the C2 modem, which will power connectivity inside the folding iPhone Duo.
This is the second-generation modem Apple has made in-house, in a move that further reduces reliance on cellular modem leader Qualcomm.
"With our fully integrated approach, it's optimized to improve everyday user experiences, including using AI algorithms to improve cellular reliability, like reconnecting faster in low coverage areas," Johny Srouji, Apple's chief hardware officer, said in the keynote video.
C2 is 50% faster than Apple's previous modem, and adds 5Gmm support in the U.S. while running at 15% lower energy, according to Srouji.
Chip analyst Ben Bajarin told CNBC in an interview that Apple will likely eliminate Qualcomm chips altogether in next year's iPhone 19 line.
Apple stock down during 'Surprise and Shine' event
Apple's new introductions, including Siri AI and the iPhone Duo, failed to impress markets. For almost the entire duration of the near-80-minute presentation, the company's stock price was down.
Opening at $315.49 today, it popped briefly to $318 and then quickly dropped.
Year-to-date, the stock is up about 15%.
Apple Inc.
Apple said its iPhone duo will cost $1,999, in line with competitors and lower than much of what Wall Street was expecting.
It will hit store shelves on Oct. 23.
Apple Inc.
Apple's marketing chief Joswiak said that the outer display of the Duo was 90% the screen area of the iPhone 18 Pro, and the inner display is 7.6-inches.
The phone will use a fingerprint sensor built into the side button for unlocking. Its case is made out of titanium.
Craig Federighi, senior VP of Software Engineering, said that Apple had redesigned much of its iOS software to take advantage of the two screens, moving buttons and other controls. Users can multitask with two apps at the same time and can use Apple's stylus called Pencil.
"We looked at every aspect of iOS to see how we could make it even more useful on iPhone Duo," Federighi said.
Here's Apple's foldable phone: iPhone Duo
Apple Inc.
It's official, Apple is making a foldable phone.
"For a device that plays such a central role in your life, a larger display would open up entirely new possibilities," Ternus said. "We think the best way to achieve that is with a foldable design."
He said that other foldables feel like "two phones awkwardly stuck together."
Apple's phone is about the size of a passport and has an internal and external screen.
Apple Inc.
Apple Inc.
Apple Watch did not get a price increase. Series 12 will cost $399 and up, and the Ultra 4 starts at $799. Apple also announced a new version of the Apple Watch with a ceramic case.
Apple Watch can record and summarize your conversations
Apple Inc.
Apple is making its Apple Watch Series 12 into an AI device with a new feature called Audio Intelligence.
The feature will use the Apple Watch's microphone to record conversations and allow the user to review things that were just said.
"We've all been in situations where you've missed a key detail of what someone just said and wished you could go back. Now you can use live rewind, which lets you go back in time for 15 seconds," said an Apple representative in the video.
It will also be able to summarize your important conversations with a feature called Siri Recap.
"It uses ambient listening to take high-level notes of your conversations, like takeaways from a team meeting or a parent-teacher conference. Conversations will have an Apple Intelligence-generated title, summary, and key points," Apple said.
Apple said the feature would be private and would not store audio recordings or share them with Apple.
The features will be available in beta later this year.
Apple adds lots of new health features to Apple Watch
Apple Inc.
Apple redesigned a lot of the health features in its Health iPhone app with AI-powered coaching.
"Each morning, Apple Watch analyzes your recent activity, vitals, and sleep to give you one score with a clear call on your body's capacity to take on the day," Apple's Sumbal Desai said.
It's expected to launch later this year.
More details on the A20 Pro, Apple’s first 2nm iPhone chip for better heat controls and on-device AI
A20 Pro is Apple’s first 2nm iPhone chip enabling on-device AI
Apple unveiled its new A20 Pro system on a chip for iPhone 18 Pro. It's the first high-volume smartphone processor to be made on Taiwan Semiconductor 2 nanometer, the leading chip manufacturer's most advanced node. While 2nm chips can only be made in Taiwan, Apple has committed to make some iPhone chips on TSMC's new fabs in Arizona, too.
The A20 Pro is meant to optimize AI on-device, as Apple races to catch up in the AI race by relying on the security and privacy of avoiding the cloud. The A20 Pro is a system on a chip, or SoC, with central and graphics processors and memory integrated together, and it has a dedicated AI accelerator Apple calls a Neural Engine, to optimize that AI on device.
The A20 Pro has a six-core CPU that Apple said runs up to 20% faster, with neural accelerators to power low-latency on-device AI workloads. Its new GPU has seven cores for up to a 40% increase in performance.
Memory took a big leap too, with a 50% increase in bandwidth and what Apple said is the "widest memory interface we've ever shipped in an iPhone." Apple got there by redesigning the chip to place the core logic silicon side-by-side with the memory chips.
Memory optimization is key in the midst of a global memory shortage, as all the biggest players race to secure memory supply from giants SK Hynix, Samsung and Micron. It's also why Apple raised prices on MacBooks and iPads in June.
Apple Inc.
Apple announced new AirPods models called AirPods 5.
These new devices have a longer battery life and have active noise cancellation, which previously wasn't available on the least expensive AirPods. They cost $129, and there's a version with wireless charging that retails for $149.
Apple Inc.
iOS 27 will include a new feature that allows customers to use a single phone number across multiple devices, dubbed "iPhone Handoff."
According to Kaiann Drance, vice president of iPhone Marketing, "the number is instantly active on whichever iPhone you pick up."
She added that the feature will launch with T-Mobile and Deutsche Telekom, with Verizon and EE adding support by the end of the year. More carriers will follow.
iPhone 18 Pro gets a $100 price increase
Apple Inc.
Apple's new phones will get a price increase amid a global component shortage, especially for memory.
The iPhone 18 Pro will start at $1199, Apple said. That's $100 more than last year's iPhone 17 Pro.
The iPhone 18 Pro Max will start at $1299, which is also a $100 hike.
The phones go on pre-order on Saturday and will ship on Sept. 18.
Apple introduces feature to prove photo was taken by an iPhone, not made with AI
Authenticity check in the new iPhone 18 Pro camera.
Apple inc.
Apple introduced a new feature that will enable users to confirm that a photo was taken by an iPhone camera, instead of generated by AI. The feature is called Apple Reference Image.
"Now you can prove the authenticity of a photo taken on iPhone 18 Pro. Apple Reference Image starts in the most secure way possible with the sensor. The new main camera securely signs photo data at a pixel level right at the time of capture," an Apple presenter said.
The feature won't be available in the EU or China.
Newly designed shutter will allow for better depth of field
Apple Inc.
One of the big improvements to Apple's iPhone cameras is that they now come with physical shutters that can be controlled to control depth of field, focus, and bokeh.
"To create variable aperture, we developed a system of six laser-cut blades, each thinner than a human hair," Apple VP Kaiann Drance said.
Apple Inc.
Apple says the iPhone 18 Pro has a significantly improved battery life
The new Apple CEO, John Ternus, appears at an Apple product launch event.
Andrej Sokolow | Picture Alliance | Getty Images
Apple is emphasizing improved battery life as a major selling feature of the devices. The smaller iPhone 18 Pro gets 24 hours of battery life, and its bigger sibling can manage 30 hours on a single charge.
Announced in June, Apple unveils AI-powered Siri
Siri AI was announced in June to lackluster reception. Finally, it has made its debut.
In a promotional video, the company claims that this new version of Siri is an "entirely new version of Siri" and "can take action in the apps you already use, including third-party apps."
Apple claims Siri AI works with over 300,000 apps.
Apple says that its new iPhone chip is called A20 Pro
Apple said that it redesigned the cores on its newest iPhone chip, called A20 Pro, which will ship with the new iPhone Pro. It said its redesigned cores are "desktop class" and will make artificial intelligence faster.
Apple also boasted that it is a 2nm chip. That means it's the first smartphone in the world to use the latest TSMC manufacturing technology.
Apple Inc.
Apple got its first product launch out of the way quickly.
The new iPhone 18 Pro looks a lot like last year's 17 Pro, but comes in two new colors: glacier and burgundy. It's also coming in a larger, "Max" version.
Apple Inc.
"We made massive advancements in the most important areas: intelligence, performance, battery, and camera," Ternus said.
Ternus opens by making the case that the iPhone is the best device for AI
Apple CEO John Ternus takes the stage at an Apple Event on Sept 9th, 2026.
Ternus opened his first iPhone launch as CEO with a speech about how he sees artificial intelligence and what those kinds of devices need to be. It was reminiscent of Steve Jobs' original launch of the iPhone by describing first what a perfect device would have, then saying that it's the iPhone.
"Now, if you were designing the ideal version of this hub from scratch, how would you do it? Well, first, you would want something that is always with you, deeply personal, and able to bring intelligence to the moments when it matters most," Ternus said.
"Today, we're going to take these experiences even further with the next generation of iPhone

Amazon’s October Prime Day sale is live Oct. 6 to 7, and the best tech deals aren’t necessarily the ones with the biggest percentage off. We’re looking for discounts on devices we’d actually recommend: earbuds that stay comfortable through a commute, e-readers with responsive page turns, and creator cameras that make recording easier — not just cheaper.
Mashable’s reporters and editors test tech year-round. For Prime Big Deal Days, we’re pairing those hands-on findings with price-history checks to help you decide what’s worth buying, which upgrades are worth paying for, and where a cheaper model will do the job.
Our picks include $79 AirPods 4, the $103.99 Kindle, and $80 off Bose’s second-generation QuietComfort Ultra Headphones. Below, we explain what makes each deal useful — and the compromises to know before you check out.
SEE ALSO:
The 20+ best Prime Day deals on MicroSDs, SSDs, and hard drives: Our favorite deals to beat RAMageddon
How do we pick these deals?
A low price doesn’t automatically make a good deal. We prioritize products recommended in Mashable’s reviews and buying guides, then use price-tracking tools such as camelcamelcamel to check whether the discount is unusually good. We also compare other retailers’ listings rather than assuming Amazon has the lowest price.
Where we’ve tested a product, we explain what stood out in actual use. Where a deal is for a different size, configuration, or version, we make that distinction clear. We also flag Prime membership requirements, third-party sellers, and other conditions that could change the value of an offer.
The $79 AirPods 4 are the budget pick for iPhone users who prefer earbuds without silicone tips. They offer up to five hours of listening per charge, plus H2-powered features including Personalized Spatial Audio and Voice Isolation for calls.
One important distinction: this deal is for the version without active noise cancellation. In our AirPods 4 review, we tested the ANC model, but it's still relevant in terms of functionality. For example, the review offers useful context on the shared design: the earbuds stayed secure through flights and a treadmill run, although our reviewer experienced some discomfort after roughly eight hours of wear.
The AirPods 4 reached $69 last Black Friday, so $79 isn’t their all-time low. It's their lowest price so far in 2026 — and a reasonable buy if you want Apple’s entry-level earbuds without paying extra for noise cancellation.
The 2024 Kindle is on sale for $103.99, a 31% discount, with an option to bundle three months of Kindle Unlimited for free. It’s the pick for readers who want a small, lightweight e-reader rather than every feature in the Kindle lineup.
In Mashable’s review, Lead Shopping Reporter Samantha Mangino found that the six-inch Kindle fit easily into a small crossbody bag, turned pages quickly, and displayed crisp, high-contrast text. Its 16GB of storage gives you room for thousands of books without stepping up to a more expensive model.
The trade-offs matter: this Kindle isn’t waterproof and doesn’t have the Paperwhite’s adjustable warm light. Amazon also rates its battery life at up to six weeks, compared with up to 12 weeks for the 2024 Paperwhite models. Choose the basic Kindle for portability and price; consider a Paperwhite if you read in the bath or want more control over nighttime lighting.

If you don't need the powerful MacBook Pro's features or the price tag, you can go with the M5 MacBook Air while it's on sale for $1,099, or $200 off the normal price. Not only is it highly portable, but it also uses the M5 chip, and it stays in a moderate lane without going wild with features not everyone needs. It's a great buy for students or professionals.
Apple MacBook Air (M5, 16GB RAM, 512GB SSD)

Anker is the go-to charging brand for many tech nerds (including us), and the brand dropped some big discounts for Prime Day. You can grab the cute little Nano USB-C wall charger for under $30, and it even matches the new burgundy iPhone 18 Pro. The new Anker MagGo 2 Pro Power Bank just got its first-ever discount, and it offers 25W wireless charging.
Two of Amazon's own Fire tablets are already on sale for record-low prices ahead of Prime Big Deal Days. Take your pick from the compact Fire HD 8 with 64GB of storage — our favorite Fire tablet overall — or the big-screened Fire HD 10 with 32GB of storage, nicer cameras, and a sharper display. (Both have 13-hour battery lives.) They're now up to 53% off for Prime members.

Amazon's Fire tablets have been safe from price hikes so far, but the retailer raised the prices of all its Fire TV streaming sticks by at least $5 in August. The 4K Plus model went from $49.99 to $69.99. Nevertheless, Amazon will sell it to you for just $37.99 right now. FWIW, this is Amazon's cheapest media player with support for Dolby Vision, Dolby Atmos, Nvidia Geforce Now, and Alexa Home Theater (a surround sound feature that works with Echo devices).
Dropping to the lowest we've seen at Amazon, the Apple Watch SE 3 is down to $199. In Mashable's review of the best smartwatches, the Apple Watch SE 3 takes the cake as the best model for most people. The SE was the first Apple Watch to include an always-on display, and we're always thrilled to look down and see the stunning OLED display. Plus, the S10 chip is the same as the Ultra 3, which costs nearly $800 at full price.
The 65-inch TCL QM8L is the best QLED TV for most people, according to Leah Stodart, our former TV expert. She praised its "superb peak brightness, detailed picture quality, and fantastic glare handling." (QLED TVs in general "are ideal for people whose TV usage happens mostly in the daytime, especially watching sports," to quote her TV specs guide.)

For creators who edit beyond basic cuts, support for 10-bit color and D-Log M provides more flexibility for color grading. That’s the reason to consider this older camera: the useful features are still here, even if a newer model exists.

Ugreen Nexode Pro 10000mAh 45W Mini Power Bank

This little gadget always goes on sale during Amazon sales, and so we're hardly surprised that it's one of the retailer's Prime Day deals for October 2026. pages.title: Apple Adds Dolby Atmos Sound to Live Formula 1 Races
pages.text:
Lewis Hamilton of Great Britain driving the (44) Scuderia Ferrari SF-26 on track during the F1 Grand Prix of Bahrain in Malaysia at Sepang Circuit on Oct. 04, 2026, in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.
Apple wants Formula 1 fans to hear the roar of the engines, the squeals of the tires and the chaos of the pit lane as they’ve never heard it before.
The tech giant is partnering with Dolby Laboratories to bring its Dolby Atmos sound to F1, beginning with the U.S. Grand Prix in Austin, Texas, later this month. The companies are betting that Atmos sound, paired with Dolby Vision, will make the races more exciting and visceral than they have ever been for viewers at home.
“The sound is what makes it emotional; it is the sound that guides you through that and builds the tension,” John Couling, senior VP of entertainment for Dolby Laboratories, tells The Hollywood Reporter. “That is what Dolby Atmos will deliver.”
'Imperfect Women' Renewed for Second Season at Apple TV
'Ted Lasso' Takes the Express Lane in Season 4's Penultimate Episode
Apple, of course, is not a sports juggernaut like ESPN, nor is it pouring the same resources that, say, an Amazon Prime Video is putting into the space. Instead, the tech company has decided that whatever sports it does invest in, it wants to create the best experience possible for viewers, including video nd sound quality that is a step above what is available elsewhere.
“If you are a sports fan today, our viewpoint today is that the experience is — am going to be polite and say not easy,” says Oliver Schusser, Apple’s VP of music, sports, Apple TV and Beats. “There really has not been a lot of innovation. We went into sports a couple of years back with the intention to make a difference for the customer, this is a continuation of that journey.”
The new sound experience will be available on supported Apple devices and compatible Dolby-enabled TVs, soundbars and home theater systems, with plans to continue delivering that sound and video quality for future races. F1 is responsible for producing its races, with Apple delivering it to consumers through its tech stack.
Apple is in the first year of its F1 deal, paying an estimated $140-$150 million for the rights. Eddy Cue, the executive who oversees Apple’s services business and a devout F1 fan, said last month that viewership of races is younger, more female-skewing, and “up by significant double-digit percentage growth” compared to last year when they were on ESPN.

pages.title: Jessica Chastain Defends Calling Out Apple TV Over ‘The Savant’ Delay: 'It's OK to Be Honest'
pages.text:
Jessica Chastain Defends Calling Out Apple TV Over ‘The Savant’ Delay
Getting your Trinity Audio player ready…
Jessica Chastain stood by her decision to call out Apple TV after the streamer delayed her series “The Savant,” which is now set to premiere in spring 2027.
While talking with Net-A-Porter, Chastain was asked about her Apple TV series being postponed last year in the wake of the Charlie Kirk assassination. She called them out for making the wrong decision then and she doubled down now – shortly after the streamer announced the show would finally come out next spring.
“I felt responsible to a lot of people, to all of the actors in the series… to the real person I played, I felt accountability to her because of the sacrifices that she’s made and the difficult things she’s done to keep us all safe,” Chastain said. “I really had to go on record that I thought [the postponement] was a mistake… I learned that it’s OK to be honest.”
Skeet Ulrich Explains Why He Can't Finish His 3-Film 'Scream' Arc After Melissa Barrera Firing
She added: “You can be honest in a kind and respectful way and feel like you’re still speaking your truth, you’re still authentic to who you are without being fearful of – I don’t know – I guess of never working again. Again, women are [supposed] to feel grateful. Well, we can be grateful and we can also be honest about things. We can be both things at once.”
Last month, Apple TV announced that “The Savant” was leaving the shelf and would air in 2027. The limited series had initially been set to premiere its first two episodes back on Sept. 26, 2025 — and had even been viewed by critics beforehand — but was delayed indefinitely on Sept. 23, three days before its debut.
While the streaming service did not elaborate on its reasoning behind the delay, it appeared to have been done out of sensitivity toward the assassination of Kirk on Sept. 10, 2025. Following the initial news of the delay, Chastain took to social media to explain to her fans that she fought to keep the series from being delayed.
“I’ve never shied away from difficult subjects, and while I wish this show wasn’t so relevant, unfortunately it is. ‘The Savant’ is about the heroes who work every day to stop violence before it happens, and honoring their courage feels more urgent than ever,” Chastain wrote at the time.
A representative for Apple TV did not immediately respond to TheWrap’s request for comment.

pages.title: Everything Apple Announced: iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro, Apple Watch, AirPods 5  | WIRED
pages.text:
It’s a brand-new era for Apple. The company is turning over leadership for the first time in 15 years, with former CEO Tim Cook handing off the reins last week to the new CEO, former Apple VP of hardware John Ternus.
At the first Apple product soiree hosted by Ternus, the company made an even bigger change: It announced its first-ever folding device, the iPhone Duo.
The company also announced its new line of iPhone 18 Pro phones, some updates to its Apple Watch line, new AirPods, and new software capabilities powered by Siri AI.
As expected, there were no base-model iPhone 18 announcements; those are likely coming early next year. There was also no mention of Vision Pro, iPads, or Macs. Apple touted new desktop Macs in August.
Here’s everything Apple showed off today.
Apple’s first ever folding device is the Duo, a “passport-sized” foldable iPhone. It starts at $1,999 for a model with 256 GB of storage.
It’s a product category that Apple has been working toward for a decade. Now, it hopes to do that very Apple thing where it may not be the first company to the new-tech party, but it definitely aims to be the snazziest.
The Duo is a landscape style foldable, meaning it has a vertical magnetic hinge that lets you open the device like a book. Closed, it has a 5.3-inch screen on the outside. Open it up and the landscape display is 7.7 inches. The Duo is also heavy, weighing in at 254 grams, which might be a little too hefty for some users.
The Duo is made with a titanium frame and what Apple calls a “custom polymer” screen for increased durability. It runs on Apple’s proprietary A20 Pro chip (the same chip in the new Pro-model iPhone 18s) and the company’s custom C2 modem. The horizontal format also means it's capable of running iPad-like apps, albeit ones that can adjust on the fly when folding the screen or setting the phone up at an angle. The Duo will also be able to work with the Apple Pencil Pro stylus.
On the back of the Duo are two 48-megapixel cameras, one standard, one for ultrawide shots. There are two 12-megapixel selfie cameras, one on the main screen and one on the inside when the screen is opened. The cameras can also capture 4K video.
Untypical of Apple, the Duo does not have Face ID. Instead, it uses a TouchID sensor in the power button. This is likely due to Apple’s desire to minimize the device’s bulk and allow for more components inside the device.
Like, for example, the massive battery. Apple says the iPhone Duo gets 31 hours of battery life, and up to 44 hours just using the smaller front screen. Storage options start at 256 GB for the base model, with options up to 2 terabytes of space. That top configuration puts the Duo at $3,199.
Expensive, yes, and very in line with Apple's upward adjustment to its prices due to the memory shortage. But Apple is also keen on enticing users to rent the most premium devices with Apple Upgrade, the leasing program the company introduced in July.
For more details about the Duo, check out WIRED’s deeper look at the company's very first foldable.
As expected, Apple is not releasing a base model iPhone this year. Instead, the company focused on highlighting its new iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max.
These look almost identical to the iPhone 17 Pro models, albeit slightly smaller. The iPhone 18 Pro is 6.3 inches, and the iPhone 18 Pro Max is 6.9 inches. They come in black, silver, glacier, and burgundy color options.
They feature Apple’s new A20 Pro chips, which have been repackaged into a silicone casing that can connect directly to the new, redesigned vapor chamber, a design flourish that aids in keeping the components from overheating and helps the phone last longer. Wireless charging is even faster, able to juice the phone up to 50 percent battery life in 15 minutes.
The iPhone 18 Pro battery is capable of up to 36 hours of video playback per charge. The 18 Pro Max gets around 45 hours of video playback.
The 18 Pro phones are also getting juiced up with a new and improved Siri AI. There is an all-new Siri AI app on the iPhone. Siri AI is rolling out as a beta in English now, and will be available in French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish in October.
The iPhone 18 models also get a number of big improvements to their cameras. The biggest: a variable aperture on the iPhone 18 Pro's 48-megapixel main camera. Users can dial in their preferred aperture, which adjusts mechanically in the lens. This opens up new possibilities for shooting in different light environments, as well as adjusting the depth of field for adding real—not digital—bokeh effects to photos.
Apple is also touting improved photography and video-capture controls, called Pro Controls, that let you change settings like white balance, aperture, and shutter speed. So if you’re a camera nerd, you have new software and hardware tools to play with.
Apple is also introducing Apple Reference Image, a watermarking tech that maintains an image the way it was originally shot. Apple refers to it as something close to “a digital photo negative” that you can reference if you need to prove a photo’s provenance.
The iPhone 18 Pro is $1,199, and the iPhone 18 Pro Max is $1,299. You can preorder the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max this Saturday, September 12. Apple says they’ll officially start selling September 18.
Apple announced some revamps to its Apple Watch. There is a reengineered Apple Watch 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4.
Both watches get new sensor arrays. Apple’s new Health Sensing System includes LEDs that measure high-frequency heart rate data as often as every five seconds. This gives wearers a constant stream of health data all day long.
The Apple Health app gets some revisions that better track sleep and show personalized guidance about your daily readiness. This is something Google’s Pixel watches have had for a while, though Apple’s reports will benefit from its new sensor array.
Also on the watch are some features that make use of Apple’s ambient listening tech to record and log the things around you. That means the watch can transcribe the things people say and show the text right on your smartwatch’s screen. In a demonstration video today, Apple showed a server at a restaurant reciting menu specials, and the person sitting at the table was able to scroll back through a transcript of the last 15 seconds on their Apple Watch’s screen to read what the server said.
These features are opt-in—at least for the person wearing the watch—and the features that record audio will emit a chime when somebody uses them. You can learn more about how the Apple Watch listens in Lily Hay Newman’s report for WIRED.
The listening feature can also send alerts to your wrist when it detects important sounds like sirens, doorbells, and babies crying. Apple says the audio is not stored, the raw audio is inaccessible even by Apple, and that the transcriptions do not identify the people talking.
There are new ceramic cases and color options for the Series 12 Watch, including gray, black, light gold, and bronze. The Apple Watch Series 12 is $399. The Apple Watch Ultra 4 is $799.
For more about the Apple Watch updates, read Boutayna Chokrane’s WIRED story about all the details.
Apple’s new, cheaper AirPods 5 come with some of the features that the AirPods 4 had. The AirPods 5 come with noise canceling and adaptive sound controls. You can also use Siri AI directly on the AirPods and communicate via chat. They also have live language translation, though it’s not clear how well that will function out in the real world—of course, it works great in Apple’s demo videos.
The base model costs $129. There’s also a version with touch volume controls on the stems, a little more battery, and a wireless case-charging puck that also can charge your Apple Watch. Those nicer options cost $149.
Some rumors had predicted that Apple would show off a new pair of AirPods with cameras in the earbuds. Those are possibly still coming eventually, but Apple didn't say anything about them this time. We’re expecting at least one more Apple event before the end of the year, and they may show up then.

pages.text:
Apple sets Q4 2026 earnings release for November 2
Apple will announce the results of its fiscal third quarter of 2026 on Monday, November 2. Here’s what to expect.
Price increases likely to play major role
Apple confirmed today that it will report its Q4 2026 earnings on Monday, November 29.
Following the release of its quarterly results, the company will host a conference call at 2:00 p.m. PT / 5:00 p.m. ET, where John Ternus is expected to participate for the first time as Apple’s new CEO, alongside Apple CFO Kevan Parekh.
For its fiscal Q4 last year, Apple reported $102.47 billion in revenue, up 8%, and $27.47 billion in profit, a whopping 87% increase compared to a $14.7 billion profit in Q4 2024, as a result of a one-time $10.2 billion tax charge related to Apple’s long-running tax dispute in Ireland.
During last quarter’s earnings, Apple said it expected revenue for fiscal Q4 2026 to grow between 9% and 11% year over year, despite an expected 2.5 percentage-point foreign exchange headwind and significantly greater supply constraints affecting the iPhone, Mac, and iPad.
If that pans out, Apple’s revenue should come in between $111.69 billion and $113.74 billion. Apple also guided for a gross margin between 47% and 48%, down from 50.1% last quarter, although that figure included a roughly two-percentage-point benefit from tariff refunds.
In practical terms, Apple’s quarterly results will offer the first full-quarter look at the impact of the sweeping price increases it introduced across much of its hardware lineup in late June.
It is also worth noting that, since the reporting period for this fiscal quarter ended in late September, the results are unlikely to provide a meaningful indication of demand for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, which also received price increases, as the new models only went on sale on September 18.
That said, Apple’s results will reveal how the company weathered another quarter of memory shortages and rising component costs, clearing the way for Ternus’s first full fiscal quarter as CEO to be reported in late January.

Apple also previously announced that it will be releasing a high-end Mac Studio configuration with the M5 Ultra chip and 512GB of RAM in "late October."
Another new product expected this October is a new iPad mini with an OLED display, an A20 Pro chip, a landscape front camera, a redesigned speaker system, and more. It is unclear if the device will be announced alongside new home products on October 13, alongside new Macs in the final week of October, or at some other point this month.
All in all, it appears that Apple has two sets of product launches planned for this October, and that is on top of the iPhone Duo launching on Friday, October 23. Get ready, as it is about to be a busy couple of weeks in the world of Apple.

We're expecting a harvest of new products from Apple this month.
Fall is a busy time for Apple, and we’re expecting a big harvest of products this October.
The highlight might be the first touchscreen MacBook. Also apparently coming in the next few weeks could be Apple’s first smart home hub. Plus, we’re keeping our eyes open for an updated HomePod mini and Apple TV 4K. If all that wasn’t enough, an OLED iPad mini and several other Macs are reportedly waiting in the wings.
And, of course, the month will bring the launch of the folding iPhone Duo, which Apple unveiled in September.
Some of these products supposedly will arrive on October 13. Others have less certain release dates, so there’s still plenty of room for surprises. Here are the new products we’re expecting out of Apple this month.
8 new Apple products coming in October 2026
Apple has been busy recently, but we’ve only seen the first fruits of what new Apple CEO John Ternus called an “incredible” product pipeline. Cupertino kicked off a Mac refresh with revamped Mac mini and Mac Studio models in August. Then September brought the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, Apple Watch Series 12, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and AirPods 5. (The iPhone Duo was announced but not released, as noted.)
Apple isn’t showing any signs of slowing down. If the rumors prove correct, we can expect as many as eight new products in October. Just note that what you are about to read is based on leaks and other unconfirmed reports. Any of it could be incorrect.
The touchscreen MacBook Pro could pack so many new features it’s a potential game-changer for Apple.
Concept image: Cult of Mac/Apple/ChatGPT
Rumors and leaks of a touchscreen MacBook Pro circulated for years, and it’s apparently finally almost here. Bloomberg reported this week that Apple could introduce it as early as October, though the launch might slip to November.
This appears to be the beginning of a new era for the MacBook Pro. Beyond the touchscreen, Apple reportedly developed 14- and 16-inch versions with an OLED display and a thinner design. Other reports indicate a Dynamic Island will replace the traditional notch.
Apple has reportedly been working to make macOS 27 touch-friendly for this notebook and its successors.
Expect an M5 Pro or M5 Max processor inside, not new M6 variants that aren’t available (and might never be).
See also: Why Apple’s touchscreen MacBook will be worth the wait
Apple’s much-anticipated smart home hub could launch in October.
Apple plans to break into a new product category with its long-rumored smart home hub. The device is expected to feature a roughly 6-inch square touchscreen designed to sit on a countertop or hang on a wall.
The hub supposedly will be built around Apple’s revamped Siri AI, allowing it to control smart home devices while also handling things like FaceTime calls, music, photos, messages and other apps. And Bloomberg says the product is coming on October 13.
For a full description of everything that has leaked so far about the device, read: Apple’s long-awaited smart home hub finally gets a launch date.
The HomePod mini 2 and updated Apple TV 4K should look much like their predecessors.
Alongside with the smart home hub, rumors point to refreshed versions of the HomePod mini and Apple TV 4K.
Both will supposedly retain their familiar designs while getting faster processors capable of supporting Apple’s new Siri AI features. Making the smart home devices AI-friendly is apparently the primary goal of these new models.
Expect them to launch at the same time as Apple’s smart home hub.
See also: What does Siri AI mean for your old HomePod?
Apple’s next MacBook Pro could arrive in October with the new M6 processor.
The standout feature of the 2026 Mac mini is the M6 processor. The latest generation of Apple silicon brings a substantial performance boost over its predecessor, with a faster CPU, a significantly more powerful GPU and a redesigned Neural Engine aimed at accelerating Apple Intelligence workloads. The M6 also delivers major gains in graphics and AI performance while improving power efficiency.
Following long-held habits, Apple plans to keep putting this base-model variant of the chip into more of its entry-level Macs. The low-end 14-inch MacBook Pro will apparently receive the M6 processor (replacing the current M5 version) while otherwise retaining the existing design.
See also: M6 MacBook Pro rumor roundup: Faster chip, familiar design.
To be clear, this does not mean Apple is about to introduce M6 Pro and M6 Max variants for premium MacBook Pro models. High-end M6 variants have reportedly been canceled, with Apple expediting the M7 series instead.
See also: Apple will skip M6 Pro and Max chips, fast-track M7 — here’s why
A 2026 iMac could arrive soon with a faster chip and fresh colors.
The colorful 24-inch iMac could be next in line for Apple’s M6 processor. The current version of Apple’s all-in-one desktop still uses the M4, so a rumored M6 version would represent a substantial jump in performance.
Rumors suggest Apple isn’t planning a major redesign, however. This looks more like a traditional chip-and-ship upgrade, potentially accompanied by new colors.
Excited? Learn more in our roundup of 2026 iMac rumors: What to expect from Apple’s next all-in-one.
The long-anticipated OLED iPad mini is almost here!
The trusty iPad mini is reportedly about to get its biggest overhaul in years. Apple is expected to replace the current 8.3-inch LCD with an OLED display. That should bring the usual OLED benefits, including deeper blacks, stronger contrast and a brighter, more vibrant picture.
The tablet will also supposedly get a processor speed boost designed to handle Apple Intelligence features. Plus, design changes should bring better water resistance.
See also: OLED iPad mini: Everything we know so far.
With two screens, the iPhone Duo isn’t like any previous iOS device.
While Apple revealed the iPhone Duo to the world last month, the folding phone actually reaches customers in October.
With its bendable OLED screen, it’s a solid break from traditional handsets. When unfolded, the device has a 7.6-inch display and measures just 4.3 mm thick. A 5.4-inch outer screen makes it usable like a conventional iPhone when closed. Apple revamped iOS 27 for this dual-screen device and future models.
The handset runs on Apple’s A20 Pro chip and features a titanium frame, a dual-battery system and a 48MP dual-camera system.
Preorders begin on October 16, with the phone officially launching on October 23.
See also: iPhone Duo merges iPhone and iPad into one brilliant device
Timing for Apple’s many October product announcements?
Information recently leaking out of company headquarters revealed that Apple plans to introduce its smart home products — the home hub and revamped HomePod mini and Apple TV 4K — on October 13.
As noted, the touchscreen MacBook Pro is also expected this month, though November is also a possibility. As for the other new Macs and the iPad mini, perhaps they’ll launch at the same time as the home hub. But they are all rumored to hit store shelves this fall.
Ed Hardy has been writing full-time about tech for 26 years, and using it for much longer than that. His intro to Apple was a Macintosh SE/30 (which he still has), but now he uses a 13-inch iPad Pro as his primary computer.
That’s because he’s a “tablet first” type of guy. Rather than use a Macbook, he connects a keyboard case to the iPad. And instead of a desktop Mac, he connects his tablet to a 27-inch display and full-size keyboard. (So don’t try to tell him that everyone has to use a Mac to be productive.)
Before coming to Cult of Mac, Ed wrote for NotebookReview, TabletPCReview and Brighthand, as well as other sites.

pages.title: Apple’s New CEO Looking to Cut Jobs and Push for Faster Product Launches
pages.text:
Apple’s New CEO Looking to Cut Jobs and Push for Faster Product Launches
John Ternus reportedly wants to make Apple leaner and faster.
Published September 29, 2026, 5:15 pm ET
© Photo by Karl Mondon / AFP via Getty Images
Less than a month after taking the reins from Tim Cook, Apple CEO John Ternus is reportedly already shaking up the company.
Bloomberg reports that Ternus is looking to make Apple leaner and speed up product development, citing people familiar with the matter.
Among the ideas under consideration are relying less on Apple’s traditional spring and fall product release cycles and eliminating some middle-management positions, according to the outlet.
Ternus has also signaled internally that Apple needs to introduce products faster and become more experimental to stay competitive in the AI era, Bloomberg reports.
The news comes just weeks after Ternus took over from Cook, who served as Apple’s CEO for 15 years. Cook is now executive chairman of the company’s board, where Apple says his responsibilities include “engaging with policymakers around the world.”
One of Ternus’ first major appearances as CEO came on Sept. 9, when he unveiled Apple’s latest lineup of products, including the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the company’s first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo.
Now, it seems Ternus may follow other Silicon Valley companies that have turned to layoffs in order to become leaner and move faster.
Uber, for example, announced earlier this month that it was cutting about 10% of its workforce, or roughly 3,300 jobs, as part of an effort to simplify the company and reduce management layers.
Other tech executives at companies like Amazon and Meta, have also cut jobs this year, arguing their companies have become too unwieldy to move and innovate quickly.
Bloomberg reports that Ternus himself has been calling for a leaner Apple for years.
Over the past two weeks, Apple’s hardware engineering division has begun cutting engineering program-management roles, affecting several managers, including roughly half a dozen directors, according to the report. The affected employees were reportedly given a few weeks to find another position inside Apple, with those who fail to do so facing layoffs later this year.
Those cuts follow another round of reductions last month that affected more than 200 positions across teams working on Siri, the Vision Pro, and AI features for the company’s devices.
Some employees believe more layoffs are still coming this year or early next year, according to Bloomberg.
Still, Ternus reportedly wants Apple to introduce products more frequently throughout the year and find more ways to generate revenue from its existing products and services.
The company already has an stacked product pipeline set for next year, including camera-equipped AirPods, its first smart glasses, and a special iPhone planned for the smartphone’s 20th anniversary.
Apple did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Quick Answer: Walmart sells MacBooks, AirPods, Apple Watches, iPads, and iPhones for every use case and budget, with prices ranging from about $99 for AirPods 4 to $699 for a new MacBook Neo with 256GB of storage. Stock skews toward previous-generation models, so that’s often where the biggest savings are. Check the model year on the listing before buying and look for items shipped and sold by Walmart to get the most out of your buying experience.
Whether you’re shopping for your first MacBook or looking to upgrade your AirPods without breaking the bank, Walmart is your one-stop-shop for everything Apple.
Walmart sells a wide variety of Apple devices and accessories, both online and in hundreds of retail stores. In addition to offering an all-in-one shopping experience, free shipping on items over $35, and potential discounts and free trials on Apple services, Walmart has a deep shelf of older-model and restored devices that check all your boxes without the high price.
Here’s a shortlist of the most popular Apple devices and exclusive perks you’ll find only at Walmart.
The Benefits of Buying Apple Products at Walmart
Convenience, selection, potential price discounts, free shipping, and promotional Apple service trials are just a few reasons why buying your Apple devices at Walmart pays off.
Same-day pickup. Order online for in-store pickup and take your device home that day
Massive selection. Choose from thousands of new and previous-generation devices and accessories online and get everything you need in one place
Free shipping. Offered on eligible orders of $35 or more, plus in-store pickup is always free
Easy returns. Most electronics can be returned within 30 days with a receipt, while standard non-electronic items have a 90-day return window
Additionally, Walmart carries new, previous-generation, and restored Apple devices, and frequently offers carrier discounts and Rollback deals on select models. Previous-generation and Walmart Restored devices can hit a sweet spot in value, pairing familiar Apple features with lower prices, making them a practical pick for families shopping for a kid's first iPhone or iPad. Restored devices also come with a 90-day or 1-year warranty.
Your Walmart purchase might also qualify for free trial offers on Apple services, like four months of Apple Music and up to three months of Apple TV+ or Fitness+.
Which Apple Device Fits Your Everyday Budget and Lifestyle?
Whether you’re a student or parent, Walmart has a competitive lineup of new, previous-generation, and Walmart-Restored iPhones, MacBooks, AirPods, Apple Watches, iPads, and more. Older and restored items are where you’ll see the biggest savings for better value (and better device).
Prepaid, Carrier-Locked, and Unlocked iPhones
Snag an iPhone 17e that works with AT&T starting at $649 ($15.25 a month for 36 months). It has a fast A19 chip, a 6.1-inch Super Retina XDR display, and 256GB storage. The iPhone 16e with an A18 chip and 128GB storage is just $349 when you sign up for the pre-paid Walmart Family Mobile plan. (Plans start at $19.88 a month for a single line.) Need a phone for your kids? An unlocked, 16GB Apple iPhone SE 16GB is a steal at $205.56, including free Apple trials, when you buy online.
With its brilliant 13-inch Liquid Retina display, an A18 Pro chip built for AI and Apple Intelligence, and up to 16 hours of battery life, the new MacBook Neo starts at an incredible $699 with 256GB storage and is an excellent entry-level MacBook for students.
Apple AirPods 4 with H2 chip-powered Voice Isolation are a steal at $99, thanks to Walmart Rollbacks. Over-ear AirPods Max 2 are just $479, delivering deep bass and crisp highs, with up to 1.5x more Active Noise Cancellation than previous generations.
You can get the new Apple Watch Series 12 with free Apple service trials, starting at $399. The older Apple Watch SE 3 also offers top-tier health-monitoring tools and is a steal for just $239. The SE 3 might be a smarter pick for anyone buying their first Apple Watch.
iPad power users can score deals like last year’s 11th Gen iPad for $449, equipped with Apple's superfast A16 processor, 128GB of storage, and 8GB of RAM. Light users and kids can get a Walmart Restored iPad 8 for $142.05, with a 10.2-inch screen and 32GB of storage.
Select Apple Products You Can Get at Walmart
Are Walmart Rollbacks and Restored Apple Products Worth Buying?
Walmart Rollbacks and Walmart Restored products are an excellent way to snag deep discounts on the Apple devices you want.
Walmart Rollbacks let you buy an item for a lower-than-usual price, without having to wait for a seasonal sale. Rollback prices typically last from 30 to 90 days and aren’t tied to any specific holiday or clearance event.
While you can find steep discounts at Walmart.com on refurbished Apple products, some are sold by third-party sellers, meaning standards can vary. Walmart Restored Apple products are part of Walmart’s official refurbished program and are always a smart money-saving option.
In addition to guaranteed battery health thresholds, like 80% or higher for phones, Walmart Restored items include a 90-day warranty, or a 1-year warranty for “Restored Premium".
Check the “sold and shipped by” section on the product page to confirm the vendor is Walmart.
How Does Walmart Compare to Buying Directly From Tech Manufacturers?
While buying from Apple may offer more variety and custom configurations, Walmart can often offer convenience, lower prices, occasional carrier discounts on iPhones, and free trial Apple services.
The big bargains are found in Walmart’s lineup of previous-generation devices. The difference between the latest Apple product and an older model is often unnoticeable to everyday users.
Additionally, the Walmart Restored lineup offers deep discounts, high quality thresholds, and warranties.
Purchases made through Walmart.com or the Walmart app often qualify for free trial offers on Apple services, which can include up to four months of Apple Music or Apple Arcade and up to three months of Apple TV+ or Fitness+.
Walmart offers a wide selection of new, previous generation, and restored Apple devices and accessories, plus exclusive perks. Shop Apple at Walmart today and save some serious dough.
What is the difference between a Walmart Rollback and a regular sale?
Rollbacks are lower prices on specific items, based on supply-chain cost reductions, and part of Walmart’s Everyday Low Pricing (EDLP) strategy, while sales rely on seasonal events to create urgency.
Are refurbished Apple items on Walmart reliable?
Yes, while you can find steep discounts on refurbished Apple devices, Walmart Restored items carry warranties and additional Walmart protections.
Can you trade in old Apple devices at Walmart?
Yes, Walmart’s online Gadgets to Gift Cards partner program lets you trade in your used Apple devices for Walmart gift cards, or use the ecoATM kiosks inside many Walmart stores for cash.
Does Walmart price match other major electronics retailers?
No, but brick-and-mortar Walmart stores will match the identical item's price listed on Walmart.com, as long as the item is sold and shipped by Walmart.
Do Apple products bought at Walmart come with a standard warranty?
Yes, new Apple products bought at Walmart come with Apple's standard one-year warranty, while Walmart Restored products come with either a 90-day or 1-year Walmart warranty, depending on the tier.

pages.title: Apple CEO John Ternus cuts managers to speed up product launches
pages.text:
Skip to navigation Skip to main content Skip to right column
Apple CEO John Ternus cuts managers to speed up product launches
Quartz · Kevin Winter / GA / Getty Images
Wed, September 30, 2026 at 10:58 AM PDT 2 min read
Apple CEO John Ternus is moving to eliminate middle-management positions and accelerate the company's product release cadence, according to Bloomberg. The changes, which Ternus has raised in internal conversations, give early indications of the direction he plans to take Apple after Tim Cook's 15-year run as chief executive.
Among the early ideas under consideration is moving away from Apple's traditional spring and fall product launch windows in favor of releases spread throughout the year, according to Bloomberg, citing unnamed sources. Ternus has communicated to colleagues that Apple needs to move faster on product introductions and adopt a more experimental mindset if it wants to hold its ground in the AI era.
Apple's hardware engineering division has already begun cutting engineering program manager roles, including roughly half a dozen directors, according to Bloomberg. Affected employees have a limited window to land alternative roles inside Apple, and anyone unable to do so faces termination before year's end. The engineering program manager role has been central to Apple's operations for decades, serving as the connective tissue between groups and keeping development schedules on track.
The overhaul also includes broader cost-cutting efforts. Bloomberg reported that Apple has carried out notable job reductions across its Siri, Vision Pro, and AI software engineering groups, with some departures linked to performance evaluations. Smaller cuts have also affected the company's Fitness+ group.
Ternus has also been examining whether artificial intelligence tools could compress development timelines and absorb responsibilities that now fall to human workers. Over the summer, Apple drew up a proposal to cut approximately 5,000 AppleCare support workers, reasoning that increasingly capable AI-driven tools could absorb a meaningful share of that workload. The company subsequently shelved the proposal and has not moved forward with it.
Ternus, 51, formally became Apple's chief executive with a compensation package targeting approximately $58 million, including a $3 million annual salary and a targeted equity award of $55 million for fiscal 2027. He joined Apple in 2001 and led hardware engineering before taking the top role, overseeing development of the iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, AirPods, and Vision Pro. Cook moved to executive chairman on the same date.
Ternus, services chief Eddy Cue, and Chief Financial Officer Kevan Parekh are also working to identify fresh ways to generate revenue as the services segment loses some of its growth momentum. That business segment posted its first sequential quarterly revenue drop since 2022, in the June period. Next year's product lineup is expected to be extensive, with camera-equipped AirPods, Apple's first smart glasses, and a redesigned iPhone set to celebrate the device's 20th anniversary.

Apple Just Gained 10% in a Month. What Will It Take for AAPL Stock to Finally Hit $350? Apple stock just outpaced the QQQ over the past month, yet the average analyst still thinks it is worth less than its current price. What has to change before the math finally points to $350? A steady monthlong climb has put a bigger round number on the radar for Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL | AAPL Price Prediction) shareholders. Apple stock is up 10% over the past month to $340 in afternoon trading, and the natural follow-up is what it would take to reach $350. Answering that requires looking past the chart to what Wall Street’s consensus expects, how Apple compares with its peers, and what Apple is actually selling. For the full-sector context, the Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ), a fund that tracks the NASDAQ 100, is up 5% over the past month to $744.21; thus, in percentage gains, the QQQ ETF trails Apple over that stretch. Meanwhile, Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) stock is up 32% over the past month to $751.41, running far ahead of Apple over the same window. Against that pace, the gain in Apple stock looks modest, even though it exceeded the fund’s advance. On the other side of the equation, Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) stock is down 0.7% over the past month to $344.17, which leaves Apple sitting in the middle of its own group. Complicating things further, the analyst consensus target on Apple stock is $328.22, which sits below the current share price. Getting Apple stock to the headline number likely requires analysts to raise that consensus first, since the level in question sits above a price the average target hasn’t yet reached. Apple Pitches the Mac for Local Artificial Intelligence Apple is positioning its newest Mac desktops to run demanding artificial intelligence models locally, saving buyers a cloud provider’s fee for each use. According to Apple, the new machines carry substantially more unified memory and bandwidth than the desktops they replace. Those upgrades matter. Large artificial intelligence models lean heavily on fast memory, and more of it lets a single computer handle work that might otherwise go to a data center. The pitch comes down to cost. For steady workloads, cloud usage bills keep accumulating, and Apple argues capable hardware makes more financial sense over time. Apple bulls argue that local artificial intelligence gives buyers a concrete reason to pay up for more powerful Macs. That would turn a cost argument aimed at cloud providers into hardware demand Apple can actually book as revenue. Steady Mac orders of that kind would give analysts a tangible reason to revise their targets on Apple stock. However, the consensus target on Apple stock sits beneath the current share price, so the headline level asks the market to pay more than the average analyst thinks Apple is worth. A single strong product showcase can generate excitement, yet Apple needs sustained buying before the analyst math changes. What it would take is consistent Mac sales. They need to show up in Apple’s results quarter after quarter, strong enough to push analysts into lifting the consensus above the current share price. Local artificial intelligence gives Apple a credible sales pitch; the next step is proving buyers act on it at scale. Investors drawn to the local artificial intelligence story should size positions reasonably, since Apple stock already trades above the average analyst target. Balancing exposure against other mega-cap holdings can limit damage if Mac demand proves less durable than hoped. Shareholders may want to watch for signs that Mac demand tied to local artificial intelligence repeats in Apple’s upcoming quarterly reports. John Ternus plans to accelerate Apple product launches
John Ternus, the new Apple CEO, plans to launch more products, more often. | Image Credit: Apple
Apple's new CEO John Ternus is reportedly pushing for a leaner organization that can move faster and experiment more aggressively. He plans to focus on engineering and push to release more products, more often.
Ternus also could move the company away from its tradition of a few monumental product launches. Rather than concentrating major product announcements into a few annual events, he supposedly wants Apple to introduce products throughout the year.
The planned changes reportedly come with layoffs and other staff reductions as Ternus shakes up the ranks at Apple.
John Ternus lives up to his rep as a 'hardware guy'
Previous Apple CEO Tim Cook focused on operations, efficiency and the enormous global machine required to turn Apple's products into a massive business that reliably cranked out revenues. But John Ternus brings a different background to the job. As Apple's former hardware engineering chief, he is fundamentally a product and engineering executive, with years of experience overseeing the development of the devices that define the company.
Now that he's in charge, Ternus appears focused on making Apple more nimble so new products move from the engineering lab to customers more quickly.
Inside the company headquarters, he's discussed plans to accelerate product development and expand the company's range of devices, according to a report published Tuesday by Bloomberg.
"Ternus has indicated that Apple must introduce products more quickly and become more experimental to remain competitive in the artificial intelligence era," according to the report. "Managers in product-development groups are being pushed to deliver more products, more frequently and on shorter timelines."
To understand what Apple's new CEO is trying to overcome, consider the company's much-rumored efforts to develop smart glasses. Apple has reportedly been working on these since at least 2024. But the latest rumors say they won't reach the market until late 2027.
Meta Ray-Ban smart glasses are a hot item, and Meta is already on the third generation of its version. Meanwhile, Apple has nothing to compete with them, and apparently won't for another year.
While Cupertino built its reputation on releasing the best products, not the first ones, the long, long development time for Apple smart glasses could be an argument that the company has become too relaxed and lacks urgency when developing new products.
Other rumored products that should break new ground for Apple in the coming months include a touchscreen MacBook, the first camera-equipped AirPods and a smart home hub. (The company reportedly put a planned AI pendant on the back burner.)
See also: Apple's not done: 3 more products coming this spring
New CEOs traditionally bring new priorities, and that generally means layoffs as companies get reconfigured to meet the new head honcho's vision.
That's apparently happening at Apple. Before becoming CEO, Ternus argued for a leaner organization for years. Now he has the authority to make it happen.
Apple's hardware engineering division allegedly recently dismissed a number of engineering program managers, according to Bloomberg.
Plus, Apple recently cut jobs in other areas, including Siri, Vision Pro and AI-related software engineering. The company also recently reduced staffing in its Fitness+ organization.

Tim Cook had enormous shoes to fill when he took over the Apple (AAPL +0.22%) CEO role from Steve Jobs in 2011. Jobs was a visionary leader, and skeptics weren't sure Cook was the right person to lead the consumer tech company into its next chapter. Fifteen years later, and the proof is in the pudding: Over Cook's tenure, the tech giant experienced massive growth as its market cap ballooned from $350 billion to approximately $4.75 trillion.
John Ternus took over from Cook on Sept. 1, and as his time at the helm of Apple begins, he faces the same sort of questions. Long-term investors want to know: Can Ternus match Cook's incredible run? How will the growth curve bend now?
New Apple CEO John Ternus. Image source: Apple.
Apple is in terrific shape, and that's both good and bad news for Ternus. The company is a well-oiled machine, but expectations will remain elevated. In its fiscal third quarter, revenue grew 16% year over year. The growth was driven by iPhone sales that rose 21.7% and services revenue that rose 12%. Total revenue reached $109.4 billion.

Ternus is inheriting a business with immense recurring, high-margin, and diversified revenue. The downside is that the company's latest revenue guidance was fairly muted -- only 9% to 11% for the current quarter -- as management anticipates intensifying supply constraints. This will mark Ternus' first challenge, and investors will closely watch how he navigates this period.
There's also the problem with China. Under Cook, Apple became extremely reliant on Chinese manufacturing. Ternus will need to work through geopolitical tensions, the need to geographically diversify its manufacturing footprint, and U.S. pressure to onshore more of its manufacturing. And there are plenty of questions about Apple's long-term position in the artificial intelligence race.
The good news is that Ternus is a 25-year Apple veteran and has had a front-row seat to all that the iPhone maker has endured over the last quarter-century. If the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra (priced at more than $2,000) are successful, those will be not only morale wins but also economic ones.
Duplicating Cook's run won't be easy. I'd expect Ternus to usher in a new era of steady, but dialed-back growth over the next several years. A return to a focus on excellent design and innovation will be the real mark of success for the engineer-turned-executive.
Apple isn't a young, scrappy tech start-up. It's one of the largest companies in the world, and its cash-generating ability is astounding. It's still worth investing in, but it's not the growth stock it once was, and that's OK.
